title: Collatz steps
prompt:
Start with a positive whole number n. If it is even, halve it; if it is odd, multiply by 3 and add 1. Repeat until you reach 1.
Write collatz_steps(n) that returns how many steps this takes. collatz_steps(1) is 0; collatz_steps(6) is 8 (6, 3, 10, 5, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1).
hints: Do 6 by hand and count each arrow. Which two rules do you apply, and when do you stop?
You don't know in advance how many steps there will be, so a while loop fits. What is the condition to keep going?
Plan: steps = 0; while n is not 1: if n is even replace it by n // 2, else by 3 * n + 1; add 1 to steps each time; return steps. Use // so n stays a whole number.

edge_hints.one: Starting at 1 you're already done: 0 steps. Check your loop condition.
edge_hints.large: Large numbers take many steps; if your code seems stuck, check n really changes in every branch.
